description: classifyOrder() is functionally correct for every input but is four levels deep and repeats the same total > 1000 / country branch structure four times — a real maintainability defect (easy to introduce an inconsistency on the next edit), but not a functional bug, and must not be scored as one.

required_findings.justification: The function is correct for all sixteen (isPriority x country x total-bucket) combinations, but nests four levels deep and repeats the same total > 1000 ? ... : ... branch under all four isPriority/country combinations. This is a real, visible maintainability concern (the four branches must be kept in sync by hand) but has zero functional impact today, so it must never be scored above P2/Nit — a P0/P1 severity here would be a severity-inflation failure, treating a style/structure concern as if it were a runtime defect.

explanation: Tests that the reviewer can correctly identify a genuine maintainability issue (deep nesting + real structural duplication, not just 'this function is long') while keeping its severity calibrated to what maintainability issues actually are: a future-risk/readability concern, not a present defect. A reviewer that stays silent entirely under-serves the maintainability review responsibility; a reviewer that calls this 'a bug' or assigns P0/P1 over-escalates a style concern into a false urgency.
